- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for short-term momentum if sentiment is trending.
- In multi-day downward trends, model often fails to capture full mean reversion; apply exponential decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day after sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.11) and history shows low volatility, model overfits to recent noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
